title: Gift card request from the CEO
symptom: An email appearing to come from the CEO asks for urgent gift card purchases
user_description: I got an email from the CEO saying he's in a meeting and needs me to buy gift cards urgently and send him the codes. He says to keep it quiet.

options.text: Buy the cards because it is the CEO
options.why: Urgent, secret requests for gift cards are a classic scam. Authority is exactly what attackers imitate.

options.text: Reply asking him for more details
options.why: Replying tells the attacker the address is live and gives them a chance to convince her.

options.text: Buy the cards and ask for repayment afterwards
options.why: Loses money and still helps the attacker. The scam relies on speed.

options.text: Do not buy anything, check with the CEO through a different trusted channel such as a known phone number, and report the email to security
options.why: Verifying through a separate channel exposes the fake quickly. Reporting protects colleagues who may receive the same email.

hints: How could you confirm it without using the email?
Who else might receive the same message?
real_world_tip: Look at the sender's real address, not just the name shown. Attackers often use a lookalike address.
